title: Rahm returns from LIV absence to claim Abu Dhabi title
text:
Rahm returns from LIV absence to claim Abu Dhabi title

Agence France-Presse

Nov 8, 2026

Add AL-MONITOR on Google

Kiss and make up: Jon Rahm returns to the DP tour with a win in Abu Dhabi — Fadel SENNA

John Rahm completed a winning return to the European tour as he held off Tyrrell Hatton by two strokes on Sunday to win the Abu Dhabi Championship.
The Spaniard was playing in his first event on the DP Tour since leaving the bankrupt LIV Golf tour last month. 
"It means a lot," Rahm, who turns 32 on Tuesday, said. "I'm almost not letting myself believe it because it's been quite a while since I played good in a DP World Tour event and my last showing, if we don't count withdrawals, I think I finished last.
"So last to first, it's a pretty good feeling."
Rahm started the day one shot ahead of Englishman Hatton and Italian Francesco Laporta, with Rory McIlroy another shot back.
Rahm had three birdies going out and three more coming home. After a bogey on the third, he did not drop another stroke, though he had a scare. 
"As far as I'm concerned, apart from the tee-shot at 17 it was a pretty flawless back nine. It was really, really solid," he said.
"After everything that's gone on and some poor play, battles mentally with the noise, to come back out after a little bit of rest and having a new addition to the family, it's special," said Rahm, who in October announced the birth of his fourth child.
After briefly surrendering the lead after McIlroy started with a birdie and an eagle, Rahm regained it on the third hole and never surrendered it though he had to share it for a while.
He was in a four-way tie with Laporta, McIlroy and Hatton as late as the 11th hole. 
Laporta dropped three shots on the next two holes and Rahm pulled clear with birdies on 12 and 15 for a final round of 67 and 23-under-par total of 265.
Hatton shot a 68 to finish two shots back and seal his place at next week's World Tour Championship in Dubai.
McIlroy was two shots further back to rise to second in the DP rankings, behind Eugenio Chacarra, who finished 22nd, in a bid for a record-equalling eighth Harry Vardon Trophy, the traditional award for the top player on the European tour.
